title: BCNF Exercises
description: Resolve overlapping candidate keys to achieve Boyce-Codd Normal Form

data.text: BCNF is a stricter version of 3NF. It requires that every determinant is a candidate key. Overlapping candidate keys or non-trivial functional dependencies on non-superkeys cause violations.

data.title: BCNF violations
items: Agent represents company, but one agent represents multiple companies
Non-key column determines another non-key column

data.title: Agent-company dependency
data.content: An agent can represent multiple companies, and a company can have multiple agents. agent determines company_name, but agent is not a candidate key.

data.title: BCNF decomposition
data.content: Decompose into agents and agent_company junction.

rows: Determinant is not a candidate key

items.question: When does 3NF fail but BCNF succeeds?
items.answer: When a non-candidate key determines another attribute. 3NF allows this if the determinant is a candidate key.

items.question: Does BCNF always preserve dependencies?
items.answer: No. BCNF decomposition can lose some functional dependencies. Use 3NF if dependency preservation is critical.

items.question: Is BCNF worth the complexity?
items.answer: For most applications, 3NF is sufficient. Use BCNF when overlapping keys cause update anomalies.

data.title: Summary
points: Ensure every determinant is a candidate key
Accept that BCNF may lose dependency preservation
Prefer 3NF when dependency preservation matters more
data.takeaway: BCNF removes subtle anomalies from overlapping candidate keys at the cost of potentially losing functional dependency preservation.
